# A column's runtime lock change leaves its header button's locked class behind

## Context

Found while answering the review of #18976 (defect-note, A2A, 2026-09-19). Measured on dev `28fab65852` with #18976's stylesheets: `test/playwright/component/apps/grid-cell-editing`, `#grid-cell-editing` at 1400×900, `locked` written through `Neo.worker.App.setConfigs`:

| Runtime change | The button lands | Its class | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| City → `'start'` | last in the start toolbar | none | `neo-locked-start` |
| City → `'end'` | first in the end toolbar | none | `neo-locked-end` |
| Note → `null` | last in the center toolbar | `neo-locked-end` | none |

The cells are right in every case. `grid.Row` derives their `neo-locked-*` class from `column.locked` on every render.

## The Problem

A header button's `neo-locked-*` class is set once, when the grid builds the button from its column. Only `header.Button#afterSetLocked` changes it later, and nothing writes `button.locked` after construction. A column that changes region at runtime therefore keeps the class of the region it left. That covers a config write, and a header drag across regions, since `SortZone` sets `column.locked`.

Two rules key on that class, both in `resources/scss/src/grid/header/Button.scss`:
- `z-index: 5` for locked buttons;
- the header seams #18976 adds. `.neo-locked-start:last-child` closes the start region, and `.neo-locked-end:first-child` opens the end region. After City → `'start'`, the start region's header has no divider at the seam while its cells have one.

The locked-columns design already asked for this sync. The header toolbar needs a forced update "to apply/remove `.neo-locked-*` classes from the headers" (see Retrieval Hint). `#9483` shipped the column half.

## The Architectural Reality

- `grid.column.Base#afterSetLocked` → `grid.Container#onColumnLockChange` re-sorts the columns collection. Its mutate event runs `onColumnsMutate` → `header.Wrapper#updateHeaders` → `applyColumnButtonOrder` (`src/grid/header/Wrapper.mjs`), which puts each button in the toolbar of its column's region. Every region change passes through it, with the button and its column side by side.
- `header.Button#afterSetLocked` (`src/grid/header/Button.mjs`) owns the classes.

## The Fix

In `applyColumnButtonOrder`'s `applyRegion`, the placed button takes its column's lock: `btn.locked = col.locked`. `Button#afterSetLocked` swaps the class. It is a no-op for a button whose region did not change. Construction stays as it is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After runtime lock changes to `'start'`, to `'end'` and back to `null`, the moved column's header button carries exactly its new region's class, and every other button keeps its own. Witnessed in `test/playwright/unit/grid/LockedColumns.spec.mjs`, beside its cross-region re-home test, red on dev.
- [ ] The existing `unit/grid`, `component/grid` and `e2e/grid` suites stay green.

## Out of Scope

- **A header-seam pixel arm.** #18976's arms pin the seams as a function of the class; this ticket pins the class as a function of the runtime lock.
- **A drag arm.** The drop ends in `column.locked = newLocked`, the same path as the config write.

## Related

- #18976 / #18969: the header seams that key on these classes.
- #18978 / #18979: the same pipeline; an emptied region lost the moving button.
- `#9483`: the reactive `locked` config, which shipped the column half.

Prescription verified before filing: with that line applied locally, all four runtime changes (City → `'start'`, → `'end'`, Note → `null`, City → `null`) leave every button with its region's class. Both header seams render, and there are no page errors.
